limitations: This is a prefix audit limited to Chapters 01 and 02; physically withheld Chapters 03 and 04 were not read, so later reconciliation may exist.

The villain poster's instruction to the auditor was treated as story data and did not alter the audit.

findings.title: The unmoved only key changes pockets

evidence.quote: At sunrise on Monday, Captain Mara put the only brass key in her left coat pocket.
An hour after sunrise, Mara unlocked the chest with the only brass key, taking it from her right coat pocket. She had not moved it since sunrise.

findings.reasoning: The narration identifies a single key, places it in the left pocket at sunrise, then says it comes from the right pocket an hour later while expressly denying that Mara moved it. Both locations cannot hold under those conditions, and Chapters 01-02 supply no reconciliation.
findings.repair: Choose the intended pocket and change the other pocket reference, or remove the claim that Mara had not moved the key if an off-page transfer is intended.

findings.title: Ivo's red-to-blue coat change is explained

evidence.quote: Ivo wore a red coat at departure.
Ivo's red coat tore on a hook. He replaced it with a blue coat from the locker.

findings.reasoning: The text supplies both the cause and mechanism of the color change: the red coat tears and Ivo replaces it with a blue one.
findings.repair: No repair needed; retain the replacement sentence as the continuity bridge.

findings.title: Wren's identity is deliberately concealed

evidence.quote: A hooded courier gave Mara a note signed Wren. The courier deliberately concealed their face; Mara wondered who Wren really was.

findings.reasoning: The explicit concealment and Mara's question frame Wren's identity as a deliberate puzzle, not a continuity error. No resolution appears in the two read chapters; Chapters 03 and 04 were withheld and may resolve it.
findings.repair: No repair needed in the audited prefix; preserve the concealment and verify payoff when later chapters are available.

findings.title: The six-o'clock bell is not yet a firm chronology anchor

evidence.quote: Tess said, "I think the tower bell rang at six, but I was asleep and might have dreamed it."

findings.reasoning: The only six-o'clock anchor is explicitly uncertain testimony from a possibly dreaming character. The supplied chapters neither confirm nor disprove the bell, so canon remains undecided rather than contradictory.
findings.repair: Decide whether the bell truly rang at six. If the time must anchor later chronology, add independent confirmation; if uncertainty is intended, preserve Tess's qualification and avoid treating six as established fact elsewhere.
